 STAT Plus Opinion Adam’s Take 
 Sellas’ experimental blood cancer immunotherapy reduced risk of death in clinical trial
 The unexpected result is good news for patients with acute myeloid leukemia
 Manage alerts for this article 
 Save this story for later 
 Share this article 
 Histopathology from patient with acute myeloid leukemia. CDC 
 By Adam Feuerstein 
 Nov. 17, 2026
 Adam Feuerstein, a senior writer and biotech columnist, is the author of Adam’s Biotech Scorecard , a subscriber-only newsletter about the crossroads of drug development, business, Wall Street, and biotechnology. 
 Adam Feuerstein 
 [email protected] Adam Feuerstein is a senior writer and biotech columnist, reporting on the crossroads of drug development, business, Wall Street, and biotechnology. He is also a co-host of the weekly biotech podcast The Readout Loud and author of the newsletter Adam’s Biotech Scorecard. You can reach Adam on Signal at stataf.54.
 It looks like I was wrong about Sellas Life Sciences and its experimental blood cancer immunotherapy. 
 On Tuesday, Sellas said the therapy, called galinpepimut-S, reduced the risk of death by 41% compared to standard treatment for patients with an advanced stage of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) — an outcome that achieved the main goal of a Phase 3 clinical trial, the company said.

 In a column published in September , I predicted galinpepimut would fail to prolong survival in the Phase 3 study.
